What to know

  • Fatty acids are hydrocarbon chains. Saturated chains have no double bonds and pack tightly; unsaturated chains have cis double bonds that create kinks and lower melting points.
  • Triglycerides store energy. Three fatty acids esterified to glycerol form a compact, anhydrous fuel with more energy per gram than carbohydrate.
  • Phospholipids form membranes. A polar head and two hydrophobic tails assemble into bilayers, with proteins embedded or attached.
  • Cholesterol stiffens and organizes membranes. It is also the precursor of steroid hormones, bile acids, and vitamin D.
  • Lipoproteins carry lipids in blood. Chylomicrons carry dietary fat; VLDL carries liver-made triglyceride; LDL delivers cholesterol to tissues; HDL returns cholesterol to the liver.

Check

check.question: Which lipoprotein carries cholesterol from the liver to peripheral tissues?
check.explanation: LDL is the main cholesterol-delivery particle. HDL returns cholesterol to the liver, and chylomicrons carry dietary fat.
